method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading; exact macro, identifier, token and formula comparison; and proposition-by-proposition replay of the order, block and density arguments. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Structural properties of models of Peano arithmetic: strict linear order and discreteness, the standard initial segment, integer-like blocks of non-standard elements, the induced dense order of blocks and the order-only isomorphism result for enumerable non-standard models.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Every non-standard model of true arithmetic is a non-standard PA-model. PA-models need not satisfy every truth about the natural numbers, but every theorem of PA holds in them; in particular their interpreted less-than relation is a strict linear order.
samples.checks: The theory inclusions, derivability-to-satisfaction implication and three strict-order clauses preserve their source directions and scopes.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Zero is least, each successor is the immediate next point, and every nonzero element has a unique predecessor. Every standard element lies below every non-standard element because anything below a standard successor must be one of finitely many numeral values.
samples.checks: The zero exception is made explicit without changing the successor claim; the finite-disjunction argument and final linear-order step remain intact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The block of a non-standard element consists exactly of points a finite standard number of successor steps away in either direction. Each block has order type like the integers, distinct blocks are disjoint, and less-than between representatives induces a well-defined strict order on blocks with the standard block first.
samples.checks: Both directions of the finite-addition characterization, all representative cases in the block-order proof and the disjointness contradiction were replayed.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Adding a non-standard element moves outside the original block. Halving a non-standard element yields a strictly lower different block, there is no greatest block, and halving the sum of representatives produces a distinct block strictly between any two ordered blocks.
samples.checks: The cancellation argument, parity alternatives and midpoint inequalities retain their hypotheses. The two averaging formulas now use the unit's defined model-addition symbol.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: When the ambient non-standard model is enumerable, its non-standard blocks form a countable dense linear order without endpoints and hence have the rational order type. Therefore the order-and-equality reducts of any two enumerable non-standard models of true arithmetic are isomorphic, though their addition and multiplication need not be.
samples.checks: The newly explicit enumerability hypothesis supplies the countability needed for the rational-order theorem, and the final conclusion remains limited to the order-and-equality language.
